definitions.explanation: The area along the side of a road or route. Commonly used to describe spectators, shops, or scenery along a parade route, marathon course, or similar path.

examples.japanese: {沿道|えんどう}に{人|ひと}が{集|あつ}まった。
マラソンの{沿道|えんどう}から{大|おお}きな{声援|せいえん}が{送|おく}られた。
examples.english: Loud cheers were sent from the roadside along the marathon route.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}の{季節|きせつ}になると、{沿道|えんどう}の{並木|なみき}が{美|うつく}しく{咲|さ}き{誇|ほこ}る。
examples.english: When cherry blossom season arrives, the trees along the road bloom beautifully.

notes:
USAGE:
{沿道|えんどう} specifically means the area along the sides of a road or route. It is very commonly used in news coverage of parades, marathons, and processions to describe where spectators gather. Compare with {道端|みちばた} (roadside), which is more casual and refers to the immediate edge of any road, while {沿道|えんどう} suggests a longer stretch along a specific route.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {沿道|えんどう}の{観衆|かんしゅう}: spectators along the route
- {沿道|えんどう}に{並|なら}ぶ: to line the roadside
- {沿道|えんどう}から{声援|せいえん}を{送|おく}る: to cheer from the roadside
- {沿道|えんどう}の{住民|じゅうみん}: residents along the road
